# China ICT running dry? (China Water Risk, April 2024) — PDF

Authors: Debra Tan, Dr CT Low. Published by: China Water Risk (CWR). Publication Date: April 2024.
NOTE: This is a PDF from a specialist NGO (China Water Risk). Key figures recovered below; full verification may need the PDF opened. (Cited in draft as a water-risk source; treat as a recognized domain authority on China water risk, but it is an NGO report — trace load-bearing figures to peer-reviewed/official sources where possible.)

## Key findings (recovered)
- ICT is one of the fastest growing power hungry & carbon intensive sectors. If left unchecked, rising carbon emissions from data centre expansion will accelerate global warming & exacerbate water scarcity. Data centres are also water intensive; they typically require water for cooling so operational risks will increase for the ICT sector along with water stress.
- We estimate China's data centre water consumption to be ~1.3bn m3 today but can rise to >3bn m3 by 2030. For perspective, ~1.3bn m3 is 1.9x the water use for households & services in Tianjin, a city of 13.7mn people.
- By 2030, China's data centre racks are expected to be 2.6x that of 2022.
- China's data centres are concentrated in the North China Plain and the Yangtze River Delta, both high-water-stress regions.
- Cooling is the dominant water use; evaporative cooling is most water-intensive.

## Notes
- NGO report (China Water Risk). Authoritative for the water-risk framing but not a primary/official source; trace the 1.3bn m3 / >3bn m3 figures to the underlying data (IDC, IEA, or peer-reviewed) where load-bearing.
